steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Food poisoning is illness caused by eating food contaminated with harmful bacteria, viruses, or toxins. | Key Fact: The main food poisoning bacteria include: Salmonella, E. coli (especially O157), Campylobacter, Staphylococcus aureus, and Clostridium perfringens. | Key Fact: Salmonella is commonly found in raw poultry and eggs; symptoms include diarrhoea, vomiting, fever, and abdominal cramps. | Key Fact: E. coli O157 is found in undercooked minced beef and unpasteurised milk; it can cause severe kidney damage (haemolytic uraemic syndrome).

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on key terms from food poisoning & food-borne illness, and one past-paper question.
